card.grading: Hidden Rust integration tests drive public APIs and the CLI under temporary HOME and XDG_* environments, covering path resolution tables, precedence, migration and permissions. The existing suite is the regression gate. Score is the fraction of hidden cases passed.

card.task: /app ships a history-less Rust workspace snapshot. The agent adds XDG Base Directory support on Linux: config, data, state and cache locations for config.toml, auth, sessions, history, logs, skills and plugins. It adds env override precedence, a legacy ~/.codex fallback, a migration command and doctor output, across the crates that touch paths.

facts.claim: openai/codex issue #1980 exists, is open, and was opened 2025-08-08 requesting XDG Base Directory support on Linux
Maintainer (bolinfest) declined changing the Linux default to $XDG_CONFIG_HOME/codex; ~/.codex stays default and CODEX_HOME is honored
No merged or open PR in openai/codex implements XDG support (no linked PRs)
Release rust-v0.163.0 exists (labelled Latest, published 15 Oct) and its notes do not mention XDG or path changes
Source pinned at commit cb00a675 (source_facts head); smoke_build used commit 2f5e242d, so the pin is inconsistent
No public complete XDG implementation for Codex found via search; no fork or package found

full_card.band: 8h tier. Claimed: frontier covers config, misses sessions/logs/skills/migration; weaker model changes config only. No dated public evidence; unverified.
full_card.build_cost: Unverified. Cold cargo build of a codex-scale workspace plus reference work estimated at 2-5 days; needs spike.

Build.why: Reference of 1500+ lines across 8 crates plus cold build, estimated 2-5 days; unverified.

spike_plan.kill_if: Build OOMs or exceeds 4h; path logic lives in one helper (one-lever); or the spec cannot give unambiguous path tables and command names.
spike_plan.pass_if: Build finishes within about 2h on 8 cores/16 GB, existing tests run deterministically, and path use spans at least 5 file kinds across several crates.
steps: In a throwaway networked Linux container, clone openai/codex at one pinned commit (resolve cb00a675 vs 2f5e242d first) and record the commit.
Install the pinned Rust toolchain and run cargo build --release for the path-touching crates; time it and note peak RSS on 8 cores/16 GB.
Run the existing test suite (cargo test) on the path-touching crates; record pass/fail per test and check it is deterministic over 2 runs.
Grep for path sources (~/.codex, CODEX_HOME, dirs/home_dir, XDG) and count distinct call sites per file kind (config, auth, sessions, history, logs, skills, plugins).
Prototype one XDG resolver and wire it into two file kinds (config and sessions); time the change to estimate the per-kind work.
Decide whether call sites cluster into 5+ kinds (multi-bucket, keep) or one helper (one-lever, kill K10).

v1.summary: The issue, repo, release and Apache-2.0 licence check out, but the upstream maintainer declined the Linux default-path change, so realism is weak and the spec must name every path table and command. The smoke probe is a Node check that never built the Rust workspace, so build cost and the 8h band are unverified; conditional pass pending the spike.

v2.note: Killed (K3). The grading surface is hand-rolled: hidden tests check our own invented path tables, migration command and doctor output. The maintainer declined the XDG default in issue #1980, so a maintainer would not accept the change, and a different valid design (different precedence, command names or table) would fail. The 135 upvotes were not found. The smoke probe ran a Node build on a Rust workspace and proves nothing, and the commit pin is inconsistent (cb00a675 vs 2f5e242d). The work is mostly rerouting path call sites, so it also risks being too easy (K8).
